about: The fields and record names that Testing Floor's collector, game SDKs, desktop app and web app agree on. This file is the single source: code reads names from it, tests fail on names it does not declare, and the public telemetry field reference is generated from it. It contains no customer data and may be copied into SDK and collector repositories.
coordinate_units: Without conversion, spatial points retain native engine units; legacy Unreal length scalars use metres, while other SDK lengths use their native units. With a declared transform, points and lengths use its output unit; directions remain unitless. Map bounds and scale must describe the same output space.

endpoint.acknowledgement: The collector answers 2xx only after the batch is written to the warehouse. Retry network failures, 408, 429 and 5xx with the same event IDs. 401 and 403 mean the analytics write key was refused. Other 4xx responses reject an invalid batch.

limits.description: Largest serialized event the collector accepts.
Largest request body the collector accepts.
Default SDK limit on objects tracked at once.
Most object samples in one tracked-objects record. A larger check is split into several records with the same time.
SDK target size for one tracked-objects record.

rules: Numbers must be finite. SDKs drop NaN and infinite values.
Null values are dropped from gameplay events. In session state, null removes a key.
Nested objects are not supported. Flatten them into dot-separated keys such as player.position.x.
GUIDs and enums are sent as strings.

request_fields.description: The game's analytics write key for the environment being tested. It is not an account API key.
When the client sent the request, as an ISO 8601 time in UTC. Either a Z suffix or a +00:00 offset is accepted.
The events in this request, each with the event fields below.

event_fields.description: A new UUID for every event. Retries reuse it, so the warehouse can drop duplicates.
The event name, such as level_started. Names beginning with $tf_ are reserved for the records listed under platform records.

When the event happened, as an ISO 8601 time in UTC. SDKs 0.5.0 and later send exactly millisecond precision with a Z suffix, such as 2026-04-19T18:32:00.000Z. A +00:00 offset and finer fractions, such as the seven digits earlier Unity SDKs wrote, are still accepted.
The wire schema version. Send 2. Version 2 adds session state and tracked-object records; version 1 events are still accepted.
One ID per game launch or editor Play run. Testing Floor shows each as one run.

A stable player ID for the person playing. Shown as the Player ID. SDKs 0.5.0 and later generate a profile ID, kept in the game's saved data, and send it unless your game sets its own. The Unreal SDK 0.4 and earlier sends it only when your game sets it.

A stable ID for the installation. Used as the Player ID when $user_id is missing. SDKs 0.5.0 and later generate it unless your game sets its own. A run with neither ID has no Player ID, so runs from the same person cannot be grouped.
Context the SDK or Testing Floor attaches. Its keys are listed under context fields.

context_fields.description: Version of the SDK that sent the event.
True when the record comes from a Play session inside the engine editor rather than a built game.
Immutable game-owned build identifier, shared by the uploaded build, SDK configuration and published maps. Distinguishes builds with the same readable version label.

The game's build version, from the engine's version setting. Left out when the engine has none. Testing Floor groups and filters runs by it as the game's app version unless the game's telemetry settings name another field.
Engine name and version, such as Unity 6000.3.7f1.

The operating system family: Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, tvOS, visionOS, Web, PlayStation, Xbox or Switch, or the engine's platform name for anything else. Unity SDKs before 0.5.0 sent engine names such as WindowsPlayer or OSXEditor.
The device or hardware model the SDK reads from the engine.
The player's language as a BCP 47 tag, such as en-US. Unity SDKs before 0.5.0 sent the system language name, such as English.
Width in pixels of the game's screen or viewport, read from the engine.
Height in pixels of the game's screen or viewport, read from the engine.
The desktop app recording this event belongs to. Links telemetry to video.
The playtest the desktop app launched the game for.
Starts at 1 for each run and increases by one for every record the SDK queues. Orders records that share a time and reveals dropped records.
On a session-state or tracked-objects record, true when the record repeats every current value instead of only changes.
The desktop app's capture ID on events Testing Floor relays for the desktop app.
The Testing Floor tester on events Testing Floor relays for the desktop app.

platform_records.name: $tf_state
platform_records.description: Session state: values that stay true until they change, such as settings, input device or equipped item. Holds only changed keys unless $tf.keyframe is true; null removes a key. Analytics can keep runs whose state ever had a value.

platform_records.name: $tf_objects
platform_records.description: Positions, removals and state of tracked objects such as NPCs, vehicles and pickups, as the parallel arrays listed under tracked-object fields.

platform_records.name: $tf_telemetry_complete
platform_records.description: Sent once per run when a recording closes, after earlier batches were acknowledged. dropped_events above zero means the recording's telemetry is incomplete.

fields.description: Events the SDK dropped for this recording.
True when the run ended before the SDK could deliver everything.

platform_records.name: $tf_session_start
platform_records.description: The desktop app launched the game without recording. Older SDKs also sent it at launch.

platform_records.name: $tf_session_end
platform_records.description: Sent by SDKs before 0.2.0 when a run ended. Read in older data only.

platform_records.name: tf_session_start
platform_records.description: Pre-release name for the run start marker. Read in older data only.

platform_records.name: tf_session_end
platform_records.description: Pre-release name for the run end marker. Read in older data only.

reserved.description: Property keys may not begin with $. The collector rejects events with $ fields it does not know, and SDKs drop such properties.

Event names beginning with $tf_ are platform records. Games must not send them; SDKs 0.5.0 and later refuse them with a warning. Earlier SDKs passed them through, so such an event can be treated as a platform record or hidden from analytics.
Early SDKs sent the recording UUID as this property. It is still read; current SDKs use $tf.recording_uuid.
Testing Floor adds the recording's ID to desktop app events it relays.

conventional_properties.description: A stable, game-owned level or map identifier. Testing Floor reads it as the level unless the game's telemetry settings name another field. Tracked-object records copy game_level.* values from the latest event, so maps and paths can split by level.
Player position on every event when a position source is registered. Feeds the player-position heatmap and the run's path.
Player position, vertical axis in Unity.
Player position.

Camera position.

without_recording when the tester played without recording.
Width of the captured display or window.
Height of the captured display or window.

sdk_events.name: $tf_player_moved
sdk_events.description: On by default once the game supplies a player or camera position. Debounced movement samples, up to ten a second, with player and camera pose; the main input for player-position heatmaps and paths.

sdk_events.name: $tf_player_teleported
sdk_events.description: Sent by the SDK's teleport helpers so paths break at the jump.

tracked_object_fields.description: Object IDs, one per sample. The game's ID, or kind#n when the game gives none.
Object kinds, such as npc, boat or pickup. Analytics offers one heatmap source per kind.
Objects removed in this record. Each removal carries its final position as a sample.
Why each object was removed: destroyed, gone, disabled, removed when the game removes an object without giving a reason, or a reason the game gives.
Objects whose state changed, one per state entry.
The state key for each entry. The key label names the object on maps.
The new value for each entry: a string, number or boolean.

derived_fields.description: In analytics, the tracked object a position belongs to. Testing Floor derives it from sample.id; do not send it.
In analytics, the tracked object's kind.
In analytics, a tracked object's position.
In analytics, a tracked object's position.
In analytics, a tracked object's position.
In analytics, the estimated seconds an object stayed at a position: until its next update or removal, bounded by the run and the selected time range.
